audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Trundle level 1 and level 6 and gave Kennen levels 4-5 and 2+ items — every one of those contradicts its own why. whys[4] calls level 6 'your biggest spike' while the row said Trundle; whys[6] says play to teamfight instead while the row said Kennen. Difficulty was 7.5/10 in an even lane.
audit.why: 50.0% over 78 games with Kennen holding 950-range poke against a 300-range Chomp. He owns 2-3, 6 and first item; Trundle owns only the late.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6 flipped in matched pairs to the packet chart (Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Kennen / Kennen / Trundle), diffRating 7.5/10 -> 6/10, and the tone moved off the hard-matchup orange.

audit.why: Level 6 and first item are Kennen's; Trundle's is the two-item sustain window. Subjugate is 120/100/80, so the rank-1 window between ults is a full two minutes.
audit.corrected: 120s written into the cooldown block and dosFull[0].d; Pillar of Ice's 21s added as the second trackable timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields credit Chomp with healing him — 'it steals your attack damage and heals him', 'his bite-stacked sustain' (twice).
audit.why: Chomp deals damage, briefly slows, and saps attack damage. It does not heal. Trundle's healing is King's Tribute (a percent of the max health of any enemy unit dying near him — including every minion in the wave) and Frozen Domain, which increases healing from all sources while he stands on it. Naming the right source matters because it tells you when Grievous Wounds actually bites.
audit.corrected: Healing attributed to King's Tribute and Frozen Domain in early, whys[5], spikes[2] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: It carries the autoReset flag on a 3.5s cooldown at 300 range, so his burst opens with an attack that comes out early — the wind-up animation is the tell, not the ability cast. For a champion with Kennen's health bar that is the difference between stepping back in time and eating the trade.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, dontsFull[2].d and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice was described as something to bait, with no statement of what it does to Kennen specifically.
audit.why: It is impassable terrain. Lightning Rush lets Kennen pass through units, but not through terrain — so a pillar dropped behind you cuts the escape that your E would otherwise buy. That is the actual reason to make him spend it first.

edits.before: Trundle's whole early game is the Q bite — it steals your attack damage and heals him, so don't trade autos into him, poke with Thundering Shuriken (Q) from max range and chip with Electrical Surge passive on-hits when you can disengage. The good news: your damage is magic, so the armor he builds does nothing, and at level 2-3 a second Q plus an activated W on a marked target can stack the third Mark of the Storm for a real stun if he oversteps to CS. Mind your energy and your fragile HP bar — one greedy step lets him bite you and walk you down.
edits.after: Trundle's whole early game is Chomp — a 300-range auto reset on 3.5s that saps your attack damage, so the wind-up animation is your cue to step back, not the cast. Poke with Thundering Shuriken (Q) from 950 and chip with Electrical Surge on-hits only when you can disengage. The good news: your damage is magic, so the armour he builds does nothing, and at level 2-3 a second Q plus an activated W on a marked target stacks the third Mark of the Storm for a real stun if he oversteps to CS. Mind your fragile HP bar — one greedy step and he walks you down.

edits.before: This is your window. At 6, Slicing Maelstrom (R) stun-locks him through his sustain, and E-in (Lightning Rush) closes the gap while applying a mark — bite or no bite, his armor stack is irrelevant to your magic burst. Bait his Pillar (E): if he wastes it as a wall you E around it, R, and chunk him before Frozen Domain (W) heal-stacking kicks in. Just respect that his Q-bite will be up — try to start the all-in with him already low on AD-steal value.
edits.after: This is your window. At 6, Slicing Maelstrom (R) stun-locks him through his healing, and E-in (Lightning Rush) closes the gap while applying a mark — his armour stack is irrelevant to magic burst. Bait Pillar of Ice (E): it is 21s at rank 1, so once he spends it you walk around it, R, and chunk him before Frozen Domain (W) heal-stacking matters. Remember Lightning Rush passes through units but never through his pillar.

edits.before: Past two items Trundle reclaims this lane: his R (Subjugate) steals a chunk of your resistances and heals him for a percent of your max HP, and your squishy caster body has nothing to answer a fed drain-tank once your own R is on cooldown. Frozen Domain plus Pillar let him stick to you and you simply can't out-DPS the heal in an extended 1v1. Close it on your 6/first-item spike or pivot to teamfights, where your AoE R peel and global threat matter far more than dueling him in the sidelane.
edits.after: Past two items Trundle reclaims this lane: Subjugate steals a chunk of your resistances and health, and the theft doubles over four seconds, so a squishy caster has nothing left once your own R is down. Frozen Domain raises his healing from every source while he stands on it, so without Grievous Wounds you cannot out-damage it in a long 1v1. Close on your 6/first-item spike or pivot to teamfights, where your AoE R peel matters far more than dueling him in the sidelane.

notes: Chomp was credited with healing him in three fields; it saps attack damage and slows, nothing more. His healing is King's Tribute (off any enemy unit dying near him, so the whole minion wave feeds it) and Frozen Domain's increased healing from all sources — which is what makes Grievous Wounds timing matter and what the page now says. Added the auto-reset tell on Chomp and the fact that Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, which Lightning Rush cannot pass through even though it passes through units. The chart contradicted five of its own seven whys; all five flipped in pairs. packet.suspectNames flags 'Use Frozen Domain' in wants.foe[2] — false positive, the ability is named correctly and 'Use' is the verb. Left alone. Carried over from the mirror and still open: disk shows 50.0% / 78 games while the packet shows 48.68% / 76 on Trundle's side — the two tables disagree and neither is in my write scope.
